snippet.text: `Lowering` holds one proposal against the fence, and `refusal()` says why it fails. It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one. `whole(report)` says whether it replaces the stored report: none is stored, it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or its verdict is stronger. A report that does not replace it is still taken when it answers `different` for a dismissed finding the stored report did not; otherwise it is refused, and the first report stands, its reason and lowering included. `after(report)` is the record that stands: the report when it replaces the stored one, and the stored report otherwise, and in both a `different` answer from either report wins, so no report takes one back. evidence.snippet: `Lowering` holds one proposal against the fence, and `refusal()` says why it fails. It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one. `whole(report)` says whether it replaces the stored report: none is stored, it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or its verdict is stronger. A report that does not replace it is still taken when it answers `different` for a dismissed finding the stored report did not; otherwise it is refused, and the first report stands, its reason and lowering included. `after(report)` is the record that stands: the report when it replaces the stored one, and the stored report otherwise, and in both a `different` answer from either report wins, so no report takes one back. [The decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) sets this out.

A later round, [run 46105212847](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/actions/runs/46105212847), found that the rule also froze a claim's sameness answers. A verifier that answered `same` for a dismissed finding, then read further and answered `different` at the same verdict, was refused, and the live finding inherited the dismissal against its last judgement. The maintainer ruled on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session, that `different` from any report of a claim wins ("A"). 9f6a71f54 makes it so: `VerificationRecord.after` keeps a `different` answer from either report, a later report at an equal or weaker verdict is taken for a `different` answer the stored report lacks and keeps nothing else, and `report_verdict` says only that answer was kept. Before the fix, each new test failed at 63751cb04 for the reported reason: the correcting report was refused, and in `restatement.test.ts` the restated finding left the attention set. [The second inventory](2026-11-28-pr-658-different-wins-mutants.json), over 63751cb04...9f6a71f54 with claims in `packages/core/src/verification.ts` and `packages/pipeline/src/findings.ts`, lists 54 mutants in those files: 49 claim a kill by a named test, one is equivalent, and four are string mutants the configuration ignores. All 49 were run by hand at 9f6a71f54, each against its named test alone, which passed unmutated with one test collected and failed mutated.

- `different` wins because a `same` answer carries a human's dismissal to a live finding and takes it out of the blocking set. Under the first rule alone, a verifier that answered `same`, read further and answered `different` could not undo the first answer, and at confirmed nothing could: the finding inherited the dismissal against the verifier's last judgement. Letting `different` win keeps [the dismissal decision](2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md)'s fail-closed path, where a `different` answer leaves the finding live. A `same` after a `different` still cannot carry the dismissal.

A verifier that wants to correct its own reason at the same verdict cannot. It can only send a stronger verdict. Nothing is stronger than confirmed, so a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier: a later confirmed report that holds the claim at the lens's severity is refused, and the claim stays one step down. Under the old rule that later report won, and the claim went back up. The maintainer accepted this cost on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A, and read"), since the lowering still needs evidence at the head and passes the fence. A refused report is an error the verifier reads, and a verifier that never sends an accepted report leaves its claim unjudged, so the review reads not reviewed, as it does today for any claim the verifier skips.

# Pull request 658 keeps a claim's first verifier report

Builder agent, for [pull request #658](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/658) and [issue #657](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/657).

A verifier that reported one claim twice lost its first report: a later unlowered report at an equal verdict replaced it whole, so a placeholder reason such as "Duplicate placeholder; see the lowered report." became the finding's only reason and could undo a lowering. The maintainer agreed both changes on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session. `VerificationRecord.refusal` in core now refuses a later report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger, and takes a replay of the stored one; `upsertVerification` applies it in the report's commit, so a refused report writes nothing. `report_verdict` refuses a lowering with no evidence at the head in `prepareArguments`, before anything is stored, so the verifier can send its one report again. [The decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) replaces the old rule, and the tests and verifier goldens that pinned it change with it, as the pull request lists. The failing tests came first, in 5f24cce08; the fix is 2947dccb0, and 181057aa8 moves the goldens and the older tests to the new rule. [The inventory](2026-11-28-pr-658-first-report-mutants.json) at 181057aa8 lists 47 mutants of the three trust files and `code-hashes.ts`: 37 generated and 10 string mutants the configuration ignores. All 37 claim a kill by a named existing test, and all 37 were run by hand at 181057aa8, each against its named test alone, which passed unmutated with one test collected and failed mutated.

A later round, [run 46105212847](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/actions/runs/46105212847), found that the rule also froze a claim's sameness answers. A verifier that answered `same` for a dismissed finding, then read further and answered `different` at the same verdict, was refused, and the live finding inherited the dismissal against its last j [cut at 2 KiB]

# A claim's first report stands unless a stronger verdict follows

Status: agreed by the maintainer on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("agree to both changes"), for [issue #657](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/657). Its rule that `different` wins was ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A").

Amends: [2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md](2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md), its sections "What survives: conflicting reports" and "Goldens", for the conflicting reports and the lowering refused for want of evidence
Amends: [2026-11-08-restore-verifier-clauses.md](2026-11-08-restore-verifier-clauses.md), the strongest-verdict rule it restores from the verifier task-scope and conflicting-reports decisions
Amends: [2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md](2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md), for which of a claim's reports gives the sameness answer that decides inheritance

Choice:

1. `report_verdict` refuses a second report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger than the stored one. A replay of the stored report is taken. Otherwise the first report stands: its reason, its evidence, its sameness answers and its lowering. A stronger later verdict still replaces the first report, its lowering included, as before. The refusal says which verdict is stored and any lowering it holds.
2. A sameness answer of `different`, from any report of the claim, wins over `same`, so an answer may move from same to different and never back. A later report at an equal or weaker verdict that answers `different` where the stored report did not is taken for that answer alone, and the tool says so; the rest of the first report stands. A stronger report that answers `same` where a stored report answered `different` keeps `different`. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A"), on the round's finding that a first `same` could not be taken back.
